execution_policy: ISOLATED_SANDBOX_ONLY; no VPS, self-hosted VPS runner, or production-host test execution
observed_anchors: Current main executable_ir_adapter admits linux.process.spawn.v0::(Int)->Int only; String process signature is not admitted.
Current main ClayVM serializes UTF-8 String constants but OP_HOSTCALL rejects every non-Int argument with TYPE_TRAP.
Current main HostProcessVMHost bridges one Int request id to an immutable tuple[str,...] request and does not yet expose Clay-visible argv Bytes.

Draft PR #741 proposes provenance-bound Clay Bytes through CLAYVM/2; draft PR #744 proposes a narrow path-only String hostcall. Both remain blocked on an actually-started isolated full-repository gate.
hypothesis: A general direct Linux argv boundary can safely be modeled as Clay String values without losing host argument identity.
counterhypothesis: Linux argv can contain non-NUL byte sequences that are not valid UTF-8; collapsing the direct effect boundary to Unicode String would either reject valid host arguments or introduce implicit codec semantics, so general argv requires an opaque Bytes-preserving representation and explicit String encoding.
discriminator: Launch a child with shell=false and a single non-UTF8 bytes argument, then read /proc/self/cmdline in the child and compare the exact raw argument bytes with the parent's input while also recording Python's sys.argv reconstruction.

exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment.name: NON_UTF8_ARGV_BYTE_PRESERVATION
exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment.rollback: Ephemeral child process and temporary local files only; no product/runtime state mutation.

primary_reference_basis: Linux man-pages execve(2): argv is passed as char* strings terminated by null pointers; embedded NUL is not representable as an element.
Linux man-pages proc_pid_cmdline(5): process command line is exposed as NUL-separated strings.
Python subprocess/os documentation: POSIX process arguments and OS boundaries may use bytes; str/bytes conversion uses the filesystem encoding/error handler where applicable.
fusion_requirements: When PR #741 and PR #744 or successors are composed, preserve nominal String-versus-Bytes separation at the hostcall signature boundary.
Define general argv elements as provenance-bound owned immutable Bytes or an equivalent explicit byte-string type with NUL rejection before the Linux boundary.
Any String-to-argv conversion must be an explicit codec operation with named encoding/error policy; do not silently use Python filesystem decoding/encoding as Clay language semantics.
Keep shell=false for direct argv effects; shell semantics must remain a separately named/effect-authorized path.
Preserve the independent hostcall declared-return-type fence identified by the PR #744/#741 fusion work.
next_discriminating_implementation: Against one reviewed fusion head, add an ordinary regression (new unusual count zero) that proves a Clay Bytes argv element containing 0x80 reaches the no-shell host process boundary byte-exact while the path-only String signature cannot acquire Bytes authority. Then run canonical checker -> executable IR -> single ClayVM -> ClayOS process effect -> exact one-file EntityOS rebuild/self-test/copy-run in an actually-started isolated full-repository sandbox.
